name: Vansen ArcSafe Insulated Shock Glove MK-3
description: Bulky, high-visibility yellow outer shell over a triple-layer dielectric inner — outer is abrasion-resistant neoprene, middle is cross-linked foam dielectric rated to 40kV, inner is moisture-wicking antimicrobial jersey. Knuckle ridge and finger backs are reinforced with hard polycarbonate. Two wide hook-and-loop straps close the cuff over most standard forearm chrome, with a rubberized port-seal ring that prevents arc-flash ingress at the chrome junction.
functionality: 40kV dielectric rating. Arc-flash resistant neoprene outer. Chrome-compatible cuff with rubberized port-seal ring prevents electrical ingress at aug junctions. Polycarbonate knuckle guards for impact. Moisture-wicking inner for extended wear.
what_it_says: You work with live current and you've read the incident report from the last person who didn't.
story_hooks: A pair recovered from a substation sabotage scene has the port-seal ring deliberately cut — whoever wore these wanted current to reach the chrome.
Counterfeit MK-3s have been circulating on the Shelf; the dielectric layer is rated only to 4kV, and three workers have already been hospitalized.
A chrome-armed electrician refuses to use any other glove and has worn the same pair for four years — the outer shell is patched with duct tape but the dielectric still tests clean.

physical_description.visual_profile: Heavy-duty industrial gloves with an unmistakably utilitarian stance. Bright safety yellow dominates the silhouette, creating an immediate high-visibility presence. The cuff extends well past the wrist, designed to interface with augmented limbs. Knuckles and finger backs show pronounced hard-shell ridging that reads as armor-lite.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately oversized and bulky to accommodate multiple material layers and standard chrome augmentation forearms. The cuff is loose and adjustable via wide straps, allowing fit over various prosthetic wrist diameters. Glove body is intentionally roomy to avoid compression of underlying circuitry.
physical_description.primary_material: Outer: abrasion-resistant neoprene in high-visibility yellow. Middle: cross-linked foam dielectric rated to 40kV. Inner: moisture-wicking antimicrobial jersey. Reinforcement: hard polycarbonate on knuckles and finger backs.
physical_description.texture: Outer surface is slightly tacky neoprene with a subtle grip texture. Knuckle and finger ridges feel rigid and molded. Interior jersey is soft and brushed. Cuff straps are rubberized with hook-and-loop texture for tactile grip during fastening.
physical_description.color_scheme: High-visibility safety yellow as primary. Black rubberized accents at cuff straps and port-seal ring. Understated gray or off-white antimicrobial jersey visible at palm interior.
physical_description.closures: Two wide hook-and-loop (Velcro-style) adjustable straps at the cuff. Rubberized port-seal ring at the chrome junction provides mechanical seal rather than additional fastening.
distinctive_features: Rubberized port-seal ring designed to prevent arc-flash ingress at chrome-flesh junction
Hard polycarbonate knuckle and finger-back armor plating
Oversized cuff designed to fit over standard augmented forearms
Triple-layer dielectric construction visible as distinct material transitions at cuff edge
Manufactured branding (Vansen Industrial Safety) embossed or printed on dorsal palm
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional / working-class industrial. Issued or purchased by mid-tier factory workers, field technicians, and chrome-maintenance personnel.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by anyone interfacing with high-voltage equipment or handling chrome augmentation repairs. Signals technical competence and workplace safety compliance. Common in factory floors, substations, corpo maintenance bays, and illegal chop-shops alike.
physical_description.condition_typical: Typically broken-in but well-maintained. Outer neoprene may show minor abrasion scuffs from regular handling. Interior jersey retains antimicrobial properties. Hook-and-loop straps show moderate wear but remain functional. No significant patching unless heavily used.
